messages:
Evelyn: heads-up -- seeing a wave of tiny gpu pods bouncing between Pending and Evicted in ap-southeast1 after the inter-az packing tweak. They land, then immediately fail attach and get evicted. Anyone else?
Marcus: +1. Alerts show 'Attach rate exceeded' on several nodes and kubelet logs have a bunch of 'attach throttled by controller' entries. This started ~30m after the scheduler change that prefers remote racks when packing density high.
Nora: can you paste a stripped describe for one of the pods?
Evelyn: pasted below:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   4m    default-scheduler  0/96 nodes are available: 14 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 22 too many of requested nic attachments, 60 node(s) had untolerated taint.
  Normal   Scheduled          3m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/tiny-trace-11 to rack-03-node-07
  Warning  FailedAttach      90s   kubelet            rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = attach call throttled
  Normal   Evicted           10s   eviction-controller  NodeAffinity mismatch -> Evicted
```

Marcus: interesting: scheduler schedules remote -> attach-controller gets many concurrent requests and starts throttling. Our attach path has a per-node rate limiter that we didn't expect to be hit.
Nora: telemetry shows attach QPS spiked from 200/s to 900/s on racks 1-4 after the change. The attach worker process is hitting syscall CPU spikes and the driver init is slower after the kernel patch.
infra-bot: node/rack-03-node-07 attach-controller queue depth = 42, rate limit = 30/s, throttled_count = 128 in last 10m
Evelyn: ops mitigation proposal: 1) temporarily revert inter-az preferRemote scoring in ap-southeast1, 2) increase attach-controller rate limit and add short burst tokens, 3) add scheduler soft-scoring for nic_attach_headroom (score penalty not absolute), 4) instrument a node-level token-bucket resource so scheduler can account for attach capacity. Thoughts?
Marcus: revert +1 for quick relief. For forever-fix I'd prefer the token-bucket resource exposed as 'attach.tokens' with node capacity so scheduler can natively consider it. But that's a bit heavier change. Short-term we can bump controller limit and add jittered retries in the attacher (2 retries, 100-300ms).
Nora: agree. Also we should mark racks with hot attachers with a temporary 'attach-hot' label so scheduler will avoid them until the controller scales.
deploy-bot: scheduler/remote-pack-flag reverted in ap-southeast1 (deploy id: d-2026-0601-19). See https://ci.redwood/run/13001 :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: attach-controller replicas scaled: rack-01..rack-04 -> 3 -> 6 (scale action id: s-2026-0601-01)
Marcus: after revert + scale, attach QPS and throttles dropped within ~8 minutes. Evictions decreased from ~7/min to ~0.8/min in the last 15m.
Evelyn: follow-ups: Marcus -> open RFC for 'attach.tokens' resource and scheduler integration; Nora -> attach-controller PR for burst tokens + retry jitter; I'll add a runbook entry: if tiny pod evictions spike, check attach throttle metrics and revert remote-pack flag as emergency mitigation.
Nora: I'll also file a kernel-driver ticket with infra-hw about the recent init latency regression. Could be the 5.15.42 build rolled last week.
Evelyn: thanks team. leaving thread for PR links and the postmortem. :thumbsup:
